identity.title: List of Dutch Pokémon home video releases

source.sourceCategory: Category:Lists of animation home video releases

leadText:
The following is a list of all of the home video releases of the Pokémon animated series and s. All DVDs are Region 2.

The publishers are Bridge Entertainment Group (animated series), Universal Pictures (movies), E1 Entertainment (movies), and Warner Bros. (movies). RCV Entertainment was renamed E1 Entertainment, a subsidiary of Entertainment One Group, in 2009.

The first three movies were released by Warner Bros. with the voice actors from the Dutch dub of the animated series. From the fourth movie on the movies were distributed by RCV Entertainment, they longer included Pikachu shorts and switched to another, cheaper dubbing studio. Nearly all voice actors were replaced, the only remaining voice actors were Christa Lips (Ash) and Marlies Somers (Misty). In the fifth, sixth and seventh movie they also replaced the voice actors of Ash and Misty. From the eighth movie on they premiered on Jetix (later Disney XD) instead of DVD, this also meant that all movies from now on had the voice actors from the animated series.
plainText:
The following is a list of all of the home video releases of the Pokémon animated series and s. All DVDs are Region 2.

The publishers are Bridge Entertainment Group (animated series), Universal Pictures (movies), E1 Entertainment (movies), and Warner Bros. (movies). RCV Entertainment was renamed E1 Entertainment, a subsidiary of Entertainment One Group, in 2009.

The first three movies were released by Warner Bros. with the voice actors from the Dutch dub of the animated series. From the fourth movie on the movies were distributed by RCV Entertainment, they longer included Pikachu shorts and switched to another, cheaper dubbing studio. Nearly all voice actors were replaced, the only remaining voice actors were Christa Lips (Ash) and Marlies Somers (Misty). In the fifth, sixth and seventh movie they also replaced the voice actors of Ash and Misty. From the eighth movie on they premiered on Jetix (later Disney XD) instead of DVD, this also meant that all movies from now on had the voice actors from the animated series.

==Pokémon animated series==
All Dutch releases of the Pokémon animated series have only Dutch audio available.

===Arcade Pictures releases===
Arcade Pictures distributed these VHSes and DVDs in the Netherlands. All releases included the Kanto Pokérap in English.

 

===Bridge Pictures releases===
====VHS====

 

Bridge Pictures distributed these VHSes in the Netherlands.

 

====VHS and DVD====
Bridge Pictures distributed these DVDs in the Netherlands, at least some of them were also released on VHS.
 

=====Super de Boer=====
In 2004, the Dutch supermarket chain , in collaboration with Bridge Pictures, gave away free DVDs with one episode of a children's TV show to customers who purchased certain products, such as one kilo of beef for €3.99. Among the 30 DVDs given away were 2 single-episode Pokémon DVDs. 

 

==Pokémon movies==
===Single movie releases===
====Pokémon De Film Mewtwo tegen Mew====
 distributed the first movie in October 2002 on both VHS and DVD. Included was the first Pikachu short Pikachu's vakantie!, a trailer for the second movie, the Het verhaal van Mewtwo's afkomst short, audio commentary by Michael Haigney (director of the English edit) and Nate Grossfeld (producer), and the music video for Don't Say You Love Me by M2M. Dutch, English, French, German, and Italian audio and subtitles are available. The DVD version was reissued in 2009.

 

====Pokémon 2 Op eigen kracht====
The second movie was released by Warner Home Video in October 2002 on VHS and DVD. Included was the Pikachu short Pikachu en de redding, a trailer for the third movie, four different music videos for They Don't Understand by Dream Street, the music video for by Youngstown featuring Nobody's Angel, and the "making of" video of the soundtrack by Alysha Antonino. Dutch, English, French, German, and Italian audio and subtitles are available, while the Arabic language is only available as subtitles. The DVD was reissued in 2009.

 

====Pokémon 3 Entei in de greep van Unown====
Warner Home Video released the third movie in October 2002 on VHS and DVD. Included was the Pikachu short Pikachu en Pichu, audio commentary track "The Filmmakers Say", a "making of" video of To Know the Unknown, the music video for Pokérap GS and, a theatrical trailer. Dutch, English, French, Greek, Hebrew, and Italian audio and subtitles are available. The DVD was reissued in 2009.

 

====Pokémon 4-Ever====
RCV Entertainment distributed the fourth movie on VHS and DVD on October 1, 2003. Dutch and English audio, but only Dutch subtitles, are available.

 

====Pokémon 5: Helden====
The fifth movie was released by RCV Entertainment on March 16, 2005 on DVD. Dutch and English audio, but only Dutch subtitles, are available.

 

====Pokémon 6: Jirachi, Droomtovenaar====
The sixth Pokémon movie was released on DVD on October 1, 2005 by RCV Entertainment. Dutch and English audio, but only Dutch subtitles, are available.

 

====Pokémon 7: Doel Deoxys====
RCV Entertainment released the seventh movie on June 28, 2006 on DVD. Dutch and English audio, but only Dutch subtitles, are available.

 

====Lucario en het Mysterie van Mew====
On August 6, 2008, RCV Entertainment released the eighth movie on DVD. Only Dutch audio is available.

 

====Pokémon Ranger en de Tempel van de Zee====
The ninth movie was distributed on DVD by RCV Entertainment in September 2008. Only Dutch audio is available.

 

====De Opkomst van Darkrai====
RCV Entertainment released the tenth movie on DVD on September 1, 2009. Only Dutch audio is available.

 

====Giratina en de Krijger van de Lucht====
The eleventh movie was released on DVD on October 14, 2009 by , which had acquired RCV Entertainment in January 2008. Only Dutch audio is available.

 

====Arceus en het Juweel des Levens====
 distributed the twelfth movie on DVD on September 19, 2012. Dutch and English audio is available.

 

====Zoroark: Meester der Illusie====
The thirteenth movie was released by Universal Pictures on May 26, 2011 on DVD. Dutch and English audio is available.

 

====Pokémon de Film Wit — Victini en Zekrom en Pokémon de Film Zwart — Victini en Reshiram====
Both versions of the fourteenth movie were released together by Universal Pictures on June 13, 2012 in a two DVD box set. Dutch, German, and English audio is available.

 

====Pokémon de Film: Kyurem VS. het Zwaard der Gerechtigheid====
Universal Pictures distributed the fifteenth movie on DVD on April 24, 2013. Dutch and English audio is available.

 

===Multi-movie releases===
====Pokémon Films 4-7====
RCV Entertainment collected the fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh films into one DVD box set and released it October 18, 2006.

 

====Pokémon 4de, 5de en 6de Film====
The fourth, fifth, and sixth movies were put into a DVD box set by RCV Entertainment in 2009.

 

====Pokémon Film 8-10====
In September 2009, RCV Entertainment released the eighth, ninth, and tenth films in a DVD boxed set. The box was released earlier for visitors on August 29, 2009.
 

====Pokémon Film 4-10====
 

====Pokémon Film 1 t/m 10====
The first ten movies were collected by RCV Entertainment into a DVD box set in October 2009. All movies except 8, 9 and 10 have an English language option.

 

====Pokémon 4Ever + Helden====
On September 5, 2012, E1 Entertainment released the fourth and fifth films together in a DVD box set.

 

====Pokémon Jirachi + Doel Deoxys====
E1 Entertainment released the sixth and seventh movies in a DVD box set on September 5, 2012.

 

====Cancelled 4-7 box set====
A boxed set of the fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh movies was planned to be released October 9, 2013 by Universal Pictures Benelux, but was cancelled.

==Specials==
===Pokémon De terugkeer van Mewtwo===
Warner Home Video released the tv special Pokémon De terugkeer van Mewtwo on VHS and DVD on August 12, 2002. The Het verhaal van Mewtwo's afkomst short, a theatrical trailer, and the song Ik ben een geboren winnaar were also included. Dutch, English, and French audio and subtitles are available.

 

==References==
 

==Related articles==
